# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 28 (Bi-Vb Pc28)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc28  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 28  
**Title (English, from literature):** Giving a robe to a non-monastic  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 28, titled *Cīvaradāna* ("Giving a robe to a non-monastic"), proscribes a Buddhist nun from giving robe material meant for an ascetic (*samaṇa*) to a householder (*gahapati*), a male wanderer (*paribbājaka*), or a female wanderer (*paribbājikā*) on pain of an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) [Bechert et al. 1997; Hüsken 1997]. In the rule's narrative origin story (*nidāna*), the nun Thullanandā gives robe material intended for a *samaṇa* to performers—including actors, dancers, and acrobats [Hüsken 1997]. The text's word commentary (*padabhājanīya*) defines a *paribbājaka* as anyone who has attained the status of a religious wanderer other than Buddhist monks (*bhikkhu*) and novices (*sāmaṇera*) [Bechert et al. 1997].

 An English translation of the rule has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
